text.en: Disha sees her parents drying chillies on a mat in the sun. They say the powder will last the whole year.

Mystery 3: how do we save food from spoiling? Preserving food means keeping it safe from microbes for a long time.
Drying and dehydration: drying chillies in the Sun removes moisture. Without moisture, microbes cannot grow.
Pickling and oiling: oil poured over pickled green mango stops air from getting in, and keeps the pickle safe.
Refrigeration and freezing: fridges are too cold for microbes to grow, so cold temperature slows microbes down. A clay pot called a matka keeps water cool.
Disha's grandfather says people used salt, sugar and spices like pepper to keep food from spoiling, and we still do.
Butter needs a fridge but ghee does not, because making ghee removes the water. Heat butter, the water separates and evaporates, and ghee is ready.
In food factories food is kept in air-tight cans and packaging to keep microbes away.
Black pepper was once so popular that Vasco da Gama crossed oceans to collect it from India.
Insects preserved food long before people. Hunting wasps preserve food for their larvae.

problem.en: Which method is used for chillies, mango pickle and milk?

text.en: Chillies are dried in the Sun.
Mango pickle has oil, which keeps out air.
Milk is kept in a fridge, where it is cold.

prompt.en: Name three ways to keep food from spoiling and say how each works.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all methods work for all foods

points.en: Preserve food by removing moisture, air or warmth.
Methods: drying, oil, cold, salt and sugar.
